templates.title: Operator input to a process with more authority
templates.question: Does the process run with more authority than the operator who supplies its input?
obligations: Determine the identity the process runs as and which accounts can start it or supply input.
Show which operations use operator-supplied values while the higher authority is in effect.

templates.title: Secrets on the command line
templates.question: Are secrets accepted on the command line, where other local accounts can read the process listing?
obligations: Identify arguments that carry credentials or keys.
Show whether an alternative that keeps the value out of the process listing is offered.

templates.title: Values supplied by the operator
templates.question: Is each operator-supplied value validated before it is used as a path, size, address or option?
obligations: List the arguments and interactive inputs read and what each value is used for.
For each, locate the validation applied before use.

templates.title: What loaded code can do
templates.question: Which host functions, files and network operations are reachable from loaded code or script once it runs?
obligations: List the host functions and libraries exposed to the loaded code or script engine.
Show whether file, process and network operations are among them and how they are restricted.

templates.title: Choice of what is loaded
templates.question: Can input from outside the process, or a writable search path, choose what is loaded?
obligations: Trace the name or path argument of the load call to its origin.
Show how a relative name is resolved and which directories are searched.

templates.title: Origin of loaded code
templates.question: How is the origin of loaded code or script established before it runs?
obligations: Identify where the loaded module or script comes from and who can write to that location.
Locate any signature or digest verification made before loading.

templates.title: Run time of loaded script
templates.question: Is execution of loaded script bounded in time and memory?
obligations: Locate any instruction count, time or memory limit set on the script engine.
Show what happens when a script does not return.

templates.title: Data sent to a remote service
templates.question: What data is sent on this connection, and is the transport protected against reading in transit?
obligations: Identify the data written to this connection and whether it includes credentials or personal data.
Determine whether the connection uses an encrypted transport.

templates.title: Choice of connection destination
templates.question: Can input from outside the process choose the destination of this connection?
obligations: Trace the host, port and address arguments of this connection to their origin.
Locate any allow list or address check applied to an externally supplied destination.

templates.title: Data returned by a remote service
templates.question: Is data returned by the remote service validated before use, as input from any network peer would be?
obligations: Trace the response of this connection to its uses.
Locate the structural and bounds checks applied to the response before those uses.

templates.title: Identity of a remote service
templates.question: How does the process verify the identity of the service it connects to?
obligations: Locate certificate or key verification for this connection and the settings that control it.
Show whether verification can be switched off by configuration or input.

templates.title: Waiting on a remote service
templates.question: Is there a timeout and a response size bound on this connection?
obligations: Locate the connect and read timeouts that apply to this connection.
Show the bound on the amount of response data the process will accept.

templates.title: Environment of a process with more authority
templates.question: Does the process run with more authority than whoever sets its environment, and are environment values still trusted then?
obligations: Determine the identity the process runs as and who can set its environment.
Show which environment values are ignored or cleared when the two differ.

templates.title: Secrets in the environment
templates.question: Are secrets passed through the environment, and are they kept out of logs, child processes and error output?
obligations: Identify environment variables that carry credentials or keys.
Show whether their values are logged, echoed or inherited by spawned programs.

templates.title: Values read from the environment
templates.question: Is each value read from the environment validated before it is used as a path, size, address or option?
obligations: List the environment variables read and what each value is used for.
For each, locate the validation applied before use.

templates.title: Structure of file content
templates.question: Is the structure of file content checked (lengths, counts, offsets, nesting) before it is used?
obligations: List the fields of the file format that are used as a size, count, offset or index.
For each, locate the check that bounds it before use.

templates.title: Origin of a file
templates.question: Is the origin or integrity of the file established before its content is trusted?
obligations: Determine who can create or replace the file at the location it is read from.
Locate any signature, digest, ownership or permission check made before the content is used.

templates.title: Choice of the path that is opened
templates.question: Can input from outside the process choose which path is opened, and is the path kept inside an intended directory?
obligations: Trace the path argument of this file access to its origin.
Locate the normalization and directory check applied to an externally supplied path.

templates.title: Resource use driven by file content
templates.question: Can a file cause unbounded allocation, recursion or decompression?
obligations: Find allocations, recursion and decompression whose size depends on file content.
Show the upper bound applied to each.

templates.title: Access to a local channel
templates.question: Which local accounts can open, read or write this channel?
obligations: Identify the name, location and permissions the channel is created with.
Show which accounts those permissions admit.

templates.title: Messages from a local peer
templates.question: Is every length, count and index in a message from the channel checked before use?
obligations: List the fields of a channel message that are used as a size, count, offset or index.
For each, locate the check that bounds it before use.

templates.title: Identity of a local peer
templates.question: How is the process at the other end of the channel identified?
obligations: Identify the channel type and the permissions or credentials check applied to its peer.
Show that messages are not acted on before that check.

templates.title: Attribution of requests from the network
templates.question: Are accepted connections and the actions requested over them recorded with enough detail to attribute them?
obligations: Locate the logging performed when a connection is accepted and when a request changes state.
Show which peer attributes each record carries.

templates.title: Connection exhaustion at a listener
templates.question: What bounds the number of connections and the time a connection may stay idle or half open?
obligations: Find the connection limit, backlog and timeout settings that apply to this listener.
Show what happens to new connections once the limit is reached.

templates.title: Reach of a listener
templates.question: Which addresses and interfaces does the listener bind to, and is that reach the intended one?
obligations: Identify the bind address and port and where they are configured.
Compare the configured reach with what the documentation or deployment description intends.

templates.title: Identity of a connecting peer
templates.question: How is a connecting peer identified before its requests are acted on?
obligations: Locate the step that establishes the identity of a new connection.
Show that every request path reachable from the listener passes that step first.

templates.title: Transport protection at a listener
templates.question: Is traffic accepted on this listener protected against reading and modification in transit?
obligations: Determine whether the listener negotiates an encrypted transport and which protocol versions it accepts.
Show whether an unprotected fallback path to the same service exists.

templates.title: Completeness of a privilege change
templates.question: Is the result of each privilege change checked, and are all identities changed together and in a safe order?
obligations: List the privilege change calls and show that the result of each is checked.
Show that user, group and supplementary group identities are all changed and cannot be regained.

templates.title: Record of a privilege change
templates.question: Is each change of identity or privilege recorded, with the identity before and after?
obligations: Locate the logging performed at each privilege change call.
Show that a failed change is recorded as well as a successful one.

templates.title: Input handled before a privilege change
templates.question: Which outside input is processed while the higher authority is still in effect?
obligations: Identify the inputs read and the operations performed before the privilege change.
Show whether any of them could be deferred until after the change.

templates.title: Replies to malformed input
templates.question: What does the process send back when received data is malformed, and does the reply reveal internal state?
obligations: Locate the error paths of the receiving handler and the content of each reply.
Show whether a reply includes memory content, paths, stack traces or configuration.

templates.title: Received data reaching an interpreter
templates.question: Does received data reach a query, command, path or format interpreter without being neutralized?
obligations: Trace received data to the query, command, path and format sinks it can reach.
For each reached sink, locate the encoding, parameter binding or validation applied on the way.

templates.title: Lengths and indexes in received data
templates.question: Is every length, count, offset and index taken from received data checked against its destination before use?
obligations: List the fields of received data that are used as a size, count, offset or index.
For each, locate the check that bounds it and show the check runs before the use on every path.

templates.title: Operations a sender can trigger
templates.question: Which operations can received data trigger, and is the sender's permission checked for each?
obligations: List the state changing or privileged operations reachable from the receiving handler.
For each, locate the permission check and show it uses the established sender identity.

templates.title: Identity of the sender of received data
templates.question: How is the sender of this data identified, and is that identity checked before the data is acted on?
obligations: Locate where the sender identity is established for the handler that receives this data.
Show that the handler cannot be reached before that identity is established.

templates.title: Resource use driven by received data
templates.question: Can a peer make the process allocate, loop or wait without a bound that the receiver sets?
obligations: Find allocations, loops and waits whose size or duration depends on received data.
Show the upper bound applied to each and where that bound is set.

templates.title: Construction of a command line
templates.question: Is the command built from fixed arguments, or can outside input add arguments or shell syntax?
obligations: Trace each part of the command line to its origin.
Show whether a shell interprets the command and what quoting or argument vector is used.

templates.title: Authority given to a spawned program
templates.question: Which privileges, environment variables and open descriptors does the spawned program inherit?
obligations: List the identity, environment and descriptors in effect at the spawn call.
Show which of them are cleared or closed before the program runs.

templates.title: Output read back from a spawned program
templates.question: Is output read back from the spawned program validated before use?
obligations: Trace the output of the spawned program to its uses.
Locate the bounds and format checks applied before those uses.

templates.title: Resolution of the spawned program
templates.question: Is the program named by absolute path, or resolved through a search path an outside party can influence?
obligations: Identify how the program name is resolved to a file.
Show who can write to the directories searched.
